github.title: Shape the review body as a summary with a folded coverage block
github.author: jerridan

identity.head: 48d7dc9d5bcc46a503346c49875a287fb1e1631b
identity.description:
Shape the review body as a summary with a folded coverage block

The review body opened with one long line of counts and coverage parts that mostly said "none". A reader had to scan it for the news.

The body now has this shape:

```

## ✅ Would approve

**Tier** full. Triage: ...

| Blocking | Suggestions | Nits |
|---|---|---|
| 0 | 0 | 0 |

<details><summary>Coverage and cost</summary>

- Reviewers ran: conventions, ...
- 9 candidate findings raised, 9 dropped by the verifier
- Cost $0.70, 49 s of run time

</details>

<sub>pr-review 0.1.0</sub>
```

- The verdict is a heading with an icon. The tier and its reason follow.
- The counts are a table. The open blocking findings of earlier runs, the "Review of changes since" line and the findings outside the diff keep their places.
- The coverage is folded and lists only the parts that carry news. A part that says "none" or "0" is left out.
- The folded block adds the candidate findings and the verifier drops, the cost and the run time, all from the record.
- The check run summary uses the same table and bullets.
- The marker stays on line 1, so later runs read it as before. The table output keeps its one-line coverage.

The README section "The review body" describes the new shape. Tests in `test/github-review-body.test.ts` cover each part; six assertions in the CLI and post tests follow the new shape.

findings.claim: The new comment joins two statements with a semicolon instead of using short separate sentences.
findings.evidence: // "none" or "0" carries no news; "news" says so.
findings.suggested_fix: Split it into two sentences: "A part whose value is none or 0 carries no news. The news field tells this."
findings.explanation: CLAUDE.md rule 5 asks for ASD-STE100 prose in comments: short sentences with one statement each.

findings.claim: The open-blocking note and the 'Review of changes since' line have no blank line between them, so markdown joins them into one paragraph.
findings.suggested_fix: Push a blank line after the carried note, or before the 'Review of changes since' line.
findings.explanation: In markdown, consecutive lines with no blank line between them render as one paragraph, so the two separate statements show as a single run-on line.

findings.claim: The open-blocking line from earlier runs is followed directly by the 'Review of changes since' line, so markdown joins the two lines into one paragraph.
findings.suggested_fix: Push a blank line after the carriedNote line when it is not empty.
findings.explanation: Markdown treats two lines with no blank line between them as one paragraph, so the two notes render as one run-on sentence.

findings.claim: The design says the review body carries a coverage line, but the body now holds a folded bullet list that leaves out the empty parts.
findings.evidence: - Failures are visible. The review always posts, and its body carries a coverage line: reviewers that ran, reviewers that failed, findings dropped because a verifier call failed.
findings.suggested_fix: Say that the body carries a folded coverage block that lists the reviewers that ran and each failure or drop that occurred.
findings.explanation: After the change, the body lists only the coverage parts with news, in a folded details block, not on one coverage line.

findings.claim: The assertion on the verdict is looser than before: it no longer checks that the verdict is the heading.
findings.explanation: The tier reason or other text could contain "Would approve", so this assertion can pass even when the heading is missing.

findings.claim: No test checks the layout of the check run summary when a carried note sits before the coverage bullets, which are joined with no blank line between them.
findings.explanation: The tests check only the order of the parts. They do not check the markdown rendering, so the note can merge into the bullet list without any test failing.

first.rationale: The two lines are adjacent with no blank line between them, but this body is posted as a GitHub review comment. GitHub renders a single newline in comments as a line break, so the two notes show on separate lines and don't run together. The old code also put "Review of changes since" on its own line right after the counts line, so this PR didn't introduce the layout. The finding is at most a cosmetic suggestion.
